purpose: Gate in-memory raw subject-state daily/window features against ID342 without creating artifacts.

research_priors.read: Q1/S3 were strongest with 3-hour step-count features, Q2/Q3 with daily mobile app usage, and demographics/weekday helped across models.
The challenge exposes multimodal smartphone, wearable, proximity, GPS, light, app, and sleep-related lifelog streams for the seven Q/S targets.
Q2/Q3 are expected to respond to mobile app usage and daily routine, while Q1/S3 are expected to respond to 3-hour step, light, and sleep-boundary features.
S3 is tied to sleep onset latency, so evening and sleep-boundary phone/light/activity states are more meaningful than generic all-day averages.

decision.next_action: No row passed the strict ID342/Public-0.55 gate; keep this as negative evidence, not a candidate route.
